verses.1: And you shall make a altar of beaten stones. You shall make it from beaten stones.
verses.2: May its length be great, and may its width be vast. May its rays shine from it.
verses.3: And you saw that it was covered with pure gold on its surface, along its walls, and on its edges. You also made a golden frame around it.
verses.4: And two golden brackets will be made for him, beneath his chest. They will be placed on both sides of his body. This will serve as a way to carry him in those brackets.
verses.5: And you made the rods of iron, and you covered them with gold.
verses.6: And it was placed in front of the ark, which is on top of the altar. It’s also placed in front of the altar that’s dedicated to you.
verses.7: And Aaron lit a fire on it in the morning, after he had prepared the lamps.
verses.8: And when Aaron raises the lamps between the evenings, he shall light a permanent lamp before Jehovah for your days.
verses.9: Do not offer him any foreign or strange food, nor any gifts or offerings. Do not let them be offered to him at all.
verses.10: And Aaron shall be covered with blood once a year, as a sacrifice for his sins. It is a sacred day for you; it is a day of holiness. It belongs to Jehovah.
verses.11: And Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.12: For you will carry the heads of the Israelites on their shoulders. Each person will give his soul to Jehovah in order to carry them. There will be no one who is harmed during this process.
verses.13: This shall be given to all those who work hard, at half the weight of the sacred weight. Forty grains of weight are required for this purpose. This amount is a tribute to Jehovah.
verses.14: All that is done by those who are in charge, since forty years have passed, will be rewarded by Jehovah.
verses.15: He who is rich will not be impoverished, and he who is poor will not be reduced to half of his weight. This is so that the offering of Jehovah may be carried on your shoulders.
verses.16: And you took the money from the goods of the Israelites, and you gave it as a tribute to the Temple of God. It became a reminder for the Israelites before God’s face, as a tribute upon their hearts.
verses.17: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.18: And you made it into a pool of water, and you set it between the altar of sacrifice and the altar itself. You also poured water over it.
verses.19: And Aaron and his sons washed their hands and feet with water.
verses.20: When they come to the altar, they must wash their hands and feet before entering the sanctuary to offer sacrifices to God.
verses.21: And they washed their hands and feet, and they did not die. Thus, it became a law for them and their descendants forever.
verses.22: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.23: And you shall take for yourself five cubits of leather from the leather belt. And also, buy fifty pieces of leather.
verses.24: And five oaks were cut down at the weight of the sacred object, and also the wood of the zait.
verses.25: And you shall make it from the oil used for sacred purposes. It should be taken from the oil used for making sacred vessels. This oil will then become sacred.
verses.26: And you shall establish there the tabernacle of the Lord, and the dwelling place of the priests.
verses.27: And the altar, and all its utensils, and the menorah, and all its parts, and the altar of the incense.
verses.28: And the altar, and all its utensils, and the incense offering, and the candles.
verses.29: And you shall sanctify them; they shall be holy and unclean for anyone who touches them.
verses.30: And Aaron and his sons, you shall sanctify them to be priests to Me.
verses.31: And to the children of Israel, I will say, “The oil that is used for the sacred offerings shall be mine for your use.”
verses.32: On a man’s head, there shall be no decorations; and in his hair, nothing should be done that would make it holy. It must remain holy for you.
verses.33: A man who is like this one, and who gives something from himself to another person, will be disgraced among his own people.
verses.34: And the LORD said to Moses, “Take some ointment, balm, and honey. Also, take some hyssop and myrrh. These things shall be mixed together in a vessel.”
verses.35: And you made it into a sacred vessel, a container for holy offerings.
verses.36: And you took it from there, and you placed it before the assembly in the sanctuary that was prepared for you. It shall be a holy place for you.
verses.37: And the ritual that you shall perform in accordance with your instructions shall not be considered holy for you. It shall remain as it is: it will be for Jehovah alone.
verses.38: A man who does such things in order to smell it will be disgraced by his own people.
